newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fluctuate, no fall after Dow seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fluctuate, no fall after Dow seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares nudged down in early trade on Thursday following a fall in the Dow Jones index, but they later corrected upward.
Traders said Russian shares were overheated but forecast no falls in coming days.

At 1030 GMT, Rostelekom ordinaries fell to $4.85 from $4.91 at Wednesday's close and UES ordinaries edged down to $0.4580 from $0.4660. UES preferred shares were $0.3000 from $0.2915 and LUKoil slipped to $22.90 from $23.00.

"The market edged down in the morning as people were looking at Dow Jones, plus there were remaining sell orders from New York," Aton trader Boris Shvedsky said. "Usually if the Dow Jones goes down, people sell."
The Dow fell 119.88 points on Wednesday to 7.842,43.
"The movement is mixed and RTS (Russian Trading System) index is moving nowhere," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Corporate Securities Department Head Pavel Gronbjerg.
"There is clear support across the board. They still ask me for offer prices at these levels."
The Russian Trading System index has risen by 37.9 percent since June 3 and many traders say the market is overheated.
"What can you do if the market has gone crazy and people are bullish?" Gronbjerg said. "I am more inclined to think that we shall not have a serious correction."
Shvedsky said there was serious demand from Russian banks.

"I do not think there will be a fall today," he said. "Prices will fluctuate close to current levels. Blue chip prices are already rising partially on demand for American Depositary Receipts and partially on local demand."
He forecast rising demand for undervalued second-tier oil shares.
Yuganskneftegas rose to $22.50 from $19.50, Megionneftegaz was $8.25 after $8.22.
